Thanks again for the demo yesterday — excited to move forward. Attached is the latest Order Form (v3) and a short summary of our requested redlines related to output ownership and model training consent. Two quick asks before we progress to signature:

2) We're proposing an opt-in for training/feedback (Section 7) rather than a blanket feedback license — would Redwood accept a scoped consent for telemetry and feedback only after a commercial kickoff?

Alicia — thanks for sending and for the clear asks. Looping in Legal (Karthik) and Sales Ops (Laura) so we can get precise language back. A few immediate points: 

- Output Title: our standard is to provide customers title to outputs they generate. We typically do not transfer model weights or grant rights to retrain on customer data unless explicitly agreed.
- Training/Feedback: we offer two paths — (a) explicit opt-in where customer consents to a limited feedback license for improving hosted models, or (b) no-feedback with a price uplift and disabled telemetry.

Karthik — could you review the attached Order Form and propose verbiage for: (i) a limited output title grant; (ii) a narrow feedback license (scoped to anonymized telemetry) and a separate checkbox for training/retrain consent?

Laura — can you advise on how staged approvals would work operationally (sales signature, legal sign-off, customer countersign)? Alicia, can you share which product flows need exclusive title vs. attribution-only? That will help with drafting.

Thanks — Ill aim to get a redline by EOD Monday.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 11 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form draft — IP & training consent items to confirm

Team / Alicia,

I've reviewed v3 and sketched an internal redline (see attached: RI-redlines-training-consent.docx). Summary of recommended positions: 

- Output ownership: propose Section 4 language: "Customer retains title to Outputs generated solely by the Customer's prompts and data; Redwood retains ownership of the underlying models, weights, and improvements." This preserves customer's ability to productize outputs while protecting our model IP.
- Derivative use: add a carveout that forbids claims of ownership to Redwoods pre-existing model components and training code.
- Feedback license: recommend a two-stage clause: 
  * Stage 1 (pre-signature): no broad training consent; telemetry limited to operational metrics for SLA and billing.
  * Stage 2 (post-go-live opt-in): customer may opt into a narrow, non-exclusive, royalty-free feedback license limited to anonymized usage data for the sole purpose of improving hosted models; explicit checkbox in the order form needed.
- Training consent for custom retrain: require a separate SOW and explicit sign-off; price and timelines tied to a retrain addendum.

Risks: Heliox's ask for "exclusive title to generated outputs" is fine in our normal output language, but we must ensure downstream productization doesn't assert rights over our model artifacts (weights, tokenizer, embeddings). If they insist on ownership that extends to models derived from their prompts + our weights, we should push back.

I'll convert these bullets into redline sentences in the docx and propose a 2-line checkbox for the customer: "I consent to anonymized feedback for model improvement (optional)."

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: RI-redlines-training-consent.docx

Hi Alicia / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround. Below is a proposed path forward based on our internal redlines and ops options. Please review and let us know which option you prefer so we can provide a final order form for countersignature: 

1) Output Title: Redwood will include language that grants HelioxAI title to Outputs generated by Helioxs prompts and content. This does NOT transfer model weights, training code, or system improvements.

2) Feedback/Training: three selectable options in the order form (checkboxes): 
   - A: No-feedback (Redwood will not use Heliox data for model improvement; telemetry limited to SLA metrics; price = standard - 10% discount).
   - B: Opt-in anonymized feedback (Heliox consents post-go-live to a narrow, non-exclusive license to use anonymized telemetry for improving hosted models; default telemetry retention 90 days; standard price).
   - C: Opt-in + retrain (requires separate SOW; specifies pricing and data handling provisions).

3) Retention and audit: default telemetry retention set to 90 days; longer retention available if Heliox selects B or C (see attached SLA spreadsheet for tiers).

4) Next steps:
   - Alicia: confirm which option (A/B/C) you prefer and whether you need bespoke retention terms.
   - Ben: if Procurement needs a formal data flow diagram, we'll provide one and include redacted examples of telemetry fields.

If you confirm option B or C we will change Section 7 to include the optional checkbox and attach the SLA addendum with retention and pricing tiers. Karthik and I will produce a final redline Monday morning and route through Deal Desk for legal sign-off.

Thanks again — aiming to get this across the table early next week.

Best,
Monica Patel
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
